text:
adele: Heads up — we had a customer report: streaming sessions drop mid-response then client reconnects but can't resume. Console shows two billed sessions for the same user. Repro on canary only so far. :grimacing:
chris: which canary and which proxy?
adele: canary-3 in us-west, fronted by proxy-v2. Logs show a `204` from the proxy followed by client reconnect; resume token seems to be missing on the upstream resume request.
maya: hmm 204 from proxy means it thinks the body is empty. Any chance the proxy strips resume headers or rewrites event stream?
adele: i grepped packets — proxy drops `X-Resume-ID` header during 204 path. upstream saw a plain new connect (no resume). here's a minimal repro curl i ran against canary: ```bash
curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'X-Resume-ID: rtoken-abc123' 
  'https://canary-infer.example/realtime?model=gpt-mini' 
```
response: `HTTP/1.1 204 No Content` then client does reconnect loop.
ops-bot: incident alert created: INC-2026-3423 (stream-drop-billing-spike) :rotating_light:
kyle: console telemetry note: when resume fails we currently create a new session id and attribute to same tenant -> double-bill. We have a tag `stream.resume_attempted` but it's not surfaced in per-route billing view.
lisa: can we add a short-term guard in router: if request has `X-Resume-ID` but upstream responded 204, retry the same connection to other proxy instance before creating new session? That avoids immediate double-charge on transient 204.
achris: cautious — retrying at the edge could increase held connections and affect SLOs. Maybe better to treat 204 with resume header as "defer-close": return 499 to client and let client reconnect? Not great either.
maya: architectural note — 204 is used by proxy for short-lived keepalives when it believes no body will be streamed. But for resume flows 204 is incorrect semantics. We should ensure proxy translates to 200 with `retry: 0` and preserves resume header, or respond with a `X-Proxy-Reason` header so router knows to preserve resume.
adele: putting reproduction steps in the incident. Also saw console shows resume-success metric spike inconsistent with upstream logs (console says resumed but upstream had no resume header).
kyle: looks like console aggregation uses client-side events + route heuristics; it's inferring resume in some cases when it sees reconnect within 5s and same tenant. That inference logic is causing false-positive resume metrics.
lisa: proposal: 1) short fix: mark sessions as "resume_inferred:false" in billing if resume header missing; change UI to surface 'inferred resume' vs 'explicit resume'. 2) router change: do not strip `X-Resume-ID` on proxy 204 path (fix proxy). 3) telemetry: add `proxy.resume_header_preserved` boolean to tracing spans so console can reconcile.
achris: agreed on 1 and 2. For 3, we should add a console-level delta join: show side-by-side upstream resume header count vs console-inferred resume count for last 1h.
maya: implementation detail on proxy: it's a streaming filter that returns 204 when body is empty; filter currently clears all custom headers before early returns. We can change it to preserve any header matching `X-Resume-*`. PR small.
adele: can someone own short-term guard for billing UI? customers already pinged billing about double charge.
lisa: I can do the UI change and backend flagging. Will add a migration to mark affected sessions in the last 2h.
kyle: i'll add the span tag in router and a console query for the delta.
maya: i'll open a proxy PR to stop stripping `X-Resume-ID` and add a unit test for the 204 path. Patch will go to canary-3 first.
achris: rollout plan: proxy PR -> canary-3 -> monitor `stream.resume_header_preserved` and the inferred resume delta; if delta drops to near-zero, proceed to gradual rollout. Add a rollout-guard: block if canary error rate > 0.5% for 10m.
adele: ops-bot created deploy task: DEPLOY-8071 and assigned to maya.
ops-bot: deploy task DEPLOY-8071 status: created.
lisa: console change PR in review: https://git.internal/console/pulls/412 (adds inferred/resume flag and new billing filter).
kyle: I'll wire an ad-hoc grafana panel on the routing dashboard: `resume.header.preserved / resume.inferred` ratio. Link: https://grafana/replay/streams/resume-delta (temporary).
maya: quick note — edge case: some old SDKs don't set `X-Resume-ID` and rely on cookie-based resume. Our fix won't change those. We should keep the inferred resume metric but mark it as lower confidence.
achris: long-term: standardize resume handshake in the API: explicit `Resume-Handshake` frame in SSE initial payload rather than opaque headers. That prevents proxies from accidentally dropping it. But that's a bigger protocol change.
adele: OK action items appended to incident. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
